statement.excerpt: Consensus estimates for Microsoft’s FY2027 capex are around $186 billion in a year where its non-OpenAI/Anthropic AI revenue is expected to be $18.7 billion, meaning that even if these services had 100% net profit margins (IE: zero costs), it would take a decade of those revenues to pay back the capex.

our_interpretation: This is an observation about estimates available when the post appeared, not a prediction that actual FY2027 results will equal them.
The observation date is August 4, 2026. The underlying financial estimates concern Microsoft's fiscal year ending June 30, 2027.

The hypothetical payback calculation holds annual revenue constant, applies all of it to the stated capex, and assumes zero costs. It does not establish the actual return on Microsoft's entire investment.
The full post attributes AI revenue estimates to Wells Fargo; 'consensus' may describe only the capex estimate.
The single metric_scope represents the paired estimated flows. Each input must be verified separately before their ratio is treated as evidence.
criteria.support_condition: Independent records verify an approximately $186 billion FY2027 capex consensus and a same-year $18.7 billion estimate for the defined non-OpenAI/Anthropic AI revenue. Dividing capex by annual revenue yields approximately ten years under the stated zero-cost assumption.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous estimate records materially disagree with either quoted input, show incompatible definitions or periods, or establish that the arithmetic does not yield approximately ten years.
